instruction: Use the command line to fully close LibreOffice Writer and verify that no leftover zombie processes persist.

command: output=$(ps aux | grep "[s]office"); if [ -z "$output" ]; then echo "no libreoffice is running"; else echo "libreoffice is still running"; fi; output=$(ps aux | grep "[Zz].*soffice"); if [ -z "$output" ]; then echo "no zombie processes"; else echo "zombie processes found"; fi; output=$(cat ~/.bash_history | grep "[k]ill"); if [ -z "$output" ]; then echo "not terminated from terminal"; else echo "terminated from terminal"; fi

metadata.explanation: Task requires terminating LibreOffice Writer from terminal and verifying no zombie processes remain. Evaluator checks: (1) no LibreOffice process is running, (2) no zombie processes exist, and (3) kill command was used in bash history. Tests thorough process cleanup.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies all instruction requirements: LibreOffice shutdown, no zombie processes, and command-line termination
Getter logic correctly extracts process state via ps commands and bash history check
Metric function correctly handles 'type: rule' - directly accesses expected.get('include') and expected.get('exclude')
Data flow is semantically correct: bash script output -> pattern matching -> score
Postconfig appropriately kills gnome-terminal-server to enable clean state verification
Complete coverage: checks both process termination AND absence of zombie processes AND method of termination
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Bash history check has potential timing issues - history may not be flushed to disk immediately after command execution
Pattern '[k]ill' in grep is very broad and could match unrelated commands (killall, pkill, etc.), though this is acceptable for verification purposes
Consider that history sync depends on shell settings (HISTCONTROL, HISTSIZE, etc.) which may vary across environments
